Area.evidence_source: [009_the_interpersonal_theory_of_suicide][page/3/Text/12] Explanations for suicidal behavior at the individual level were provided in relation to three constructs highlighted by the interpersonal theory: acquired capacity to enact lethal self-harm, including violence or exposure to violence and suicidal behavior; thwarted belongingness, including loneliness and absence of reciprocal caring relations; and perceived burdensomeness, including perceived liability and self-hate (Joiner, 2007).; [009_the_interpersonal_theory_of_suicide][page/4/Text/10] All these factors are associated with suicide risk (Van Orden et al., 2010).; [009_the_interpersonal_theory_of_suicide][page/5/Text/5] Importantly, when each participant was asked directly if he or she wished to die by suicide, the answer was no—all shared a desire to live.
